heard: The first photo from Venus showed daylight bright enough to read by. On October 22, 1975, a Soviet lander touched down in the upland volcanic region of Beta-Regio. Scientists anticipated a pitch-black wasteland crushed under 90 atmospheres of pressure. Instead, the 660-kilogram armored sphere came to rest on a 20-degree volcanic slope. Sunlight filtered through dense clouds, illuminating flat, sharp-edged rocks never worn smooth by wind. Although a protective lens cover failed to separate, the lander operated for 53 minutes. Transmissions ended only when the relay orbiter drifted out of radio range below the horizon. That shocking view proved that daylight bright enough to read by existed on Venus. You
